title: Iran–Iraq War
summary: Iraq attacked Iran on 22 September 1980, beginning an eight-year war between the two neighbours. It involved chemical weapons, attacks on Gulf shipping and strikes on cities. A UN-brokered ceasefire ended the fighting in August 1988, and estimates of the dead reach about a million or more.

uncertainty.note: Start date agreed by sources; Britannica gives the end as 20 August 1988, EBSCO as 8 August 1988.

where.modern_name: Khorramshahr, Khuzestan, Iran (proxy pin for the southern front; the war spanned the whole border and the Gulf)
where.historical_name: Iran–Iraq border zone; Khorramshahr, Islamic Republic of Iran, and Ba'athist Iraq

importance.justification: Described as the longest conventional war of the twentieth century, with hundreds of thousands to over a million dead.

audience_note: Covers a war with mass casualties, child soldiers and chemical-weapons attacks on soldiers and civilians.
reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy at Khorramshahr (coordinates from a GeoNames-derived site). Britannica blocks spotcheck (403) though I read it via fetch. Sources differ on ceasefire date (8 vs 20 August 1988) and on deaths.
